conclusion.scope: GitHub issue #70 bounded Android runtime-permission reliability fault-injection slice; no security-business, security-certification, goldset, or benchmark-metric claim
conclusion.rationale: The remediated canonical accountable pair closes the prior major Settings gap. Both runs enter real Android App info, drive the visible Permissions to Location to Don’t allow path, record Don’t allow as checked and Location as no longer allowed, and then independently observe the package permission as denied. The baseline demonstrates first denial, permanent denial, grant, and post-Settings-revocation graceful degradation; the matched candidate exposes both a denial dead end and an uncaught AndroidRuntime SecurityException after Settings revocation. The candidate Journey's immediate UI observation raced the asynchronous crash, but the later checkpoint logcat and L1 verdict fail closed on the timestamped AndroidRuntime fatal exception.

gaps: The slice covers one debug-only Wikipedia fixture on one API 35 emulator, not a device/API compatibility matrix.
Android CLI cannot device-select screen capture with two online devices, so device-scoped adb supplies raw screenshots and capture manifests explicitly record annotated screenshots as unavailable.
Candidate L3 is intentionally gated after deterministic L1/L2 failures; no candidate L3 claim is made.
The candidate Journey's immediate post-tap layout did not itself observe the asynchronous crash; the subsequent canonical checkpoint logcat and L1 oracle are the authoritative crash evidence.
